ENGLISH MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ENGLISH MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.

3. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. going

4. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.

7. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .

8. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. happiness

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing writing playlets: composing playlets about a prod and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Critical Listening ● uncovering assumptions ● relat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Speaking Fluency ● sounds: ● rising-falling and fal and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Reading comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
